messages.subject: About running simulations with MplusAutomation
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am planning a simple simulation using MplusAutomation, and I have read the excellent work by Hallquist and Wiley (2018) in SEM journal. I have also looked at the Monte Carlo simulation syntax for latent class analysis. For me, the example is a bit too involved, and I wonder if there is a simpler example (such as CFA examples) that will help me understand the syntax and the steps involved.

I am currently trying to set up a simulation study using ESEM that involves nested model comparison, and I am unsure of the overall steps. I wonder if my thinking is correct below:

(1) creating datafiles (1000 in each condition)
(2) creating Mplus syntax within the directory of datafiles
(3) run all models
(4) compare all nested models (so, 1000 results within each condition)
(5) summarize results within each condition (how can I do it with MplusAutomation?)

Any pointers on how I can do this will be helpful. Thank you very much!

Best,
Chester

messages.subject: Re: remote server
messages.body_plain:
Hi Eric,

To my knowledge, you need to have Mplus running on the same machine as MplusAutomation. You may be able to hack around this somewhat if you map the drive on the server to your local machine (e.g., using sshfs or smb) -- this might allow you to access the remote data while running Mplus on the local machine. I haven't tried this, but I think it could work in principle.

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: Re: Summarizing and Comparing Model Fit Statistics
messages.subject_clean: Summarizing and Comparing Model Fit Statistics
messages.body_plain:
Hi Justin,

Rather delayed reply here, but I just wanted to mention that I have added a parser to extract ICCs from multilevel outputs. You need to install the development version: https://github.com/michaelhallquist/MplusAutomation. And then look in $data_summary in the object returned by readModels.

Best,
Michael

messages.subject: runModels on Linux - logfile
messages.body_plain:
Hello!

I'm attempting to use MplusAutomation on Linux to run a series of models.

MplusAutomation calls Mplus fine, however, it generates the following error:

> runModels("/opt/mplus/8.1", recursive=TRUE, showOutput = FALSE)
Error in file(description = logFile, open = "wt", blocking = TRUE) :
  cannot open the connection
Calls: runModels -> file
In addition: Warning message:
In file(description = logFile, open = "wt", blocking = TRUE) :
  cannot open file 'Mplus Run Models.log': Permission denied
Execution halted

This is running on Ubuntu Server 16.04 LTS (HVM), R version 3.4.4, and Mplus 8.1.

Any help is much appreciated!

Thank you!

Morgan DeBusk-Lane
